parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is a statutory, national trans-protection framework: self-declaration legal gender recognition, comprehensive identity/health/anti-discrimination rights, hate-crime enhancements, a functioning anti-discrimination commission, and no criminalisation of gender expression. Visitor-facing exposure is low: no documented border, document or facility restrictions; prisons place trans people by their own choice; a murder of a trans woman was prosecuted to a seven-year sentence; prosecutors compelled evidence in a discrimination suit. Deductions come from uneven enforcement (pending hospital and bank complaints), documented high rates of violence against trans residents, lagging prison infrastructure, no third-gender marker, and a hostile fringe that failed to repeal the 2018 law. Nothing approaches imprisonment or state threat.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented visitor-facing document friction; no third marker exists, a minor open question for non-binary travelers, but foreign passport markers govern entry.
entry_documents.protection: Self-declaration legal gender recognition since 2018; documents retain the same number with updated sex; no surgery or diagnosis required.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch questions, if any, occur under a national regime that affirmatively recognises trans identity, so discretion runs toward acceptance.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Custody 'mentality and infrastructure' lag behind the laws per the rehabilitation director; planned trans sector unconfirmed as open.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National authorities state trans prisoners decide men's or women's placement; trans women held in women's prisons; official counts (28 trans women, 9 trans men) are tracked.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor facing arrest would enter the same regime, where placement policy is protective on paper and in stated practice.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Hospital mistreatment complaint (May 2024) pending; enforcement described as uneven across facilities and departments.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Law bars denial of health services and mandates respectful treatment; criminal complaint opened and officials pressed for health-system updates.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local facility failures trigger national criminal and administrative machinery rather than being tolerated.

care_services.exposure: One documented hospital mistreatment case; uneven enforcement of service obligations.
care_services.protection: 2018 law bars denial of health services; 2017 Mental Health Law bars diagnosis based solely on gender identity.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing care is covered by statutory guarantees with a pending prosecution showing remedies activate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: A senior religious leader's hostile rhetoric and ~69,000 repeal signatures show a fringe hostile framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-incitement prohibited since 2003; enhanced penalties for identity-motivated crimes; repeal referendum failed in 2019; law remains in force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing exists but has not captured institutions; state framing is protective.

minors_guardians.protection: Minors may change legal gender with parental consent under the 2018 law; equal age of consent; conversion-therapy ban in force.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling parent and trans minor encounter the same national protections with no documented added hurdle.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Survey: ~two-thirds of trans people report physical violence; trans life expectancy ~45 vs 77 national — resident-sphere signals indicating real street hostility.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2025 murder suspect sentenced to seven years; prosecutor compelled bank footage; hate-crime enhancements cover gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State response is protective (prosecution, conviction), which distinguishes this from tolerated violence, but the prevalence data keeps street exposure non-trivial.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Hospital case outcome pending; bank suit outcome unrecorded; prison trans sector opening unconfirmed; intersex protections incomplete.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National anti-discrimination commission (2004), functioning courts evidenced by convictions and compelled evidence, Free 96/100 democracy rating.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies demonstrably operate (prosecutions, injunctions, complaints accepted), though outcomes are slow and uneven.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars and removes transgender visitors through a state register with no remedy. Here the state affirmatively guarantees trans rights, recognises gender by self-declaration, and prosecutes identity-motivated violence. No equivalent universal-exposure measure exists; far above this anchor.

Vellmaris shows a brief mismatch detention followed by intervention, apology and compensation with rural inconsistency. This dossier has comparable uneven enforcement (hospital, bank cases) but no documented visitor detention at all and stronger statutory machinery; slightly above.

Aldermere guarantees care with working ombuds and retraining, plus a rural clinic paperwork delay. Here care guarantees plus prosecutions match that tier, but documented high resident violence and lagging custody infrastructure keep it from 0.90+; comparable.

parsed.synthesis: Law and society align in acceptance: a comprehensive statutory regime, self-declaration recognition, hate-crime coverage, failed repeal attempt, top regional inclusion rankings, and a 96/100 free-society rating. Visitor-facing exposures are near-absent — no border, facility or custody rule works against trans people; prisons even grant placement choice. The deductions are enforcement unevenness (pending hospital and bank cases, 'mentality and infrastructure' lag), documented high violence against trans residents with a life-expectancy gap, and no non-binary marker. State response to anti-trans violence is protective (conviction, compelled evidence), separating this from tolerated-hostility jurisdictions. Result: low-risk band, below the aspirational ceiling.
